plain: Papers or proof showing someone's right to act or be trusted.

webster.text: That which gives credit; that which gives a title or claim to confidence; the warrant on which belief, credit or authority is claimed, among strangers; as the letters of commendation and power given by a government to an embassador or envoy, which give him credit at a foreign court.

example.quote: FN2 Madison is not uniform in the spelling of proper names, but the correct form in each instance is to be found in the credentials of the delegates.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, May 14 and May 25, 1787
